title: SparStencil: Retargeting Sparse Tensor Cores to Scientific Stencil Computations via Structured Sparsity Transformation
problem: Sparse Tensor Cores (structured 2:4 sparsity) excel at AI but underutilized for scientific stencil computations with irregular sparsity; no existing system bridges this gap
motivation: Stencil computations dominate scientific applications; enabling sparse tensor core acceleration could unlock significant performance gains for core HPC workloads
method: SparStencil takes scientific stencil computations—which typically have irregular sparse patterns—and transforms them into a format that GPU sparse tensor cores can efficiently process. It does this in three stages: first, adaptive layout morphing (a flatten-crush pipeline) restructures how the data is organized, second, it converts the irregular sparsity into structured 2:4 sparsity (where every 4 values must have at least 2 zeros) using graph matching, and third, it automatically generates optimized GPU code by searching for the best memory layout and data mapping.
key_novelty: This is the first system to use GPU sparse tensor cores for scientific stencil computations, achieving this by introducing adaptive layout morphing to transform irregular sparse patterns into 2:4 sparsity (where every 4 values has at least 2 zeros).
contributions: Adaptive Layout Morphing restructuring stencils into staircase-aligned sparse matrices
Graph matching-based sparsity transformation ensuring 2:4 compatibility
Automatic sparse MMA kernel generation with layout search
7.1x max speedup (3.1x average) on 79 diverse stencil kernels
hardware_target: NVIDIA GPUs with Sparse Tensor Cores
limitations: Requires 2:4 sparsity structure; transformation overhead not detailed; limited to structured sparsity patterns; evaluation on single GPU
